## Method

- The set of 3,007 pending claim ids equals whole-area-binding-changes.json retiredClaimIds exactly (3,007 / 3,007, no extra, none missing).
- For every row I located the native retired unit in the candidate file at 7880fbc by path and anchor, recomputed its digest (equals the registry source digest, 3,007/3,007) and proved the complete shown unit text lies byte-for-byte in the literal body of the indicated history carrier (3,007/3,007); recomputed the carrier unit digest from the HEAD file (3,007/3,007) and checked disposition move and the retirement reference in the rationale (3,007/3,007).
- Coverage in the other direction: for each of the 48 moved files every unit of the 7880fbc candidate is either a retired row or (468 units in retained files) still present at HEAD with the same digest; no unit of a moved file is unaccounted. 91 candidate units cut from the 20 retained files have no retired row: 36 were targets of manual forward rows and 49 of formerly exact rows (all rebound to history in this pass), 4 carried earlier receipts, and the last 2 are the old portal title and header fence replaced in place (preserved verbatim in the portal snapshot); I record this as an observation, not a defect.
- Verdict rule: the row is `ok` when the carriage is correct and the unit's file/section is confirmed retired; `rework`/`hold` when the file-level or section-level review (review-2whole-files.md) found the file or cut section still current or an owner question. A retired unit of a file that must stay current would not be retired at all.
